title: Knowledge check: Keys and Efficient List Updates

questions.prompt: Which approach best matches “Keys and Efficient List Updates”?
options: Put multi-step logic directly into every template expression.
Use stable, unique keys for rendered stateful list items and let directives express DOM behavior.
Use the item array index as a key for every list regardless of reordering.
Bind attributes by manually rewriting innerHTML.
questions.answer_key: Use stable, unique keys for rendered stateful list items and let directives express DOM behavior.
questions.explanation: This answer addresses Keys and Efficient List Updates directly. Verify the behavior in a small Vue 3 example and check the runtime requirements in the linked official reference.

questions.prompt: For “Purpose of the key attribute”, which practice is most reliable?
options: Give stateful rendered items stable unique keys tied to item identity, especially when items can be reordered or removed.
Always use the current array index as key even when rows can move.
Omit keys for every component rendered in a list.
Manually edit innerHTML for each list update.
questions.answer_key: Give stateful rendered items stable unique keys tied to item identity, especially when items can be reordered or removed.
questions.explanation: This practice supports the syllabus subtopic “Purpose of the key attribute”. Check the expected result and a relevant boundary or failure case.

Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.answer_key: Reproduce the state or input change, inspect the relevant Vue binding or dependency, and compare the result with the expected output.
questions.explanation: Start with a small reproducible case. Inspect the element, reactive source, Console, and expected result before changing unrelated code.
